Decision
or choice
A convenient way to make curved
arrows is to draw an ellipse, then
make the arrows to match a section
of the ellipse. When you are done you
can either delete the ellipses, or
just hide them.
Repeating the same ellipse at a
different scale, and re-using arrows
by reflecting and rotating them will
produce a more regular and cleaner
diagram, which will (hopefully) be
easy to understand.
For the curved arrows,
select the white pointer,
then use the handles to
adjust the shapes.
Label over arrow. Make tag
same colour as background.
You can use labels like these when you need
to point to something, or when you need to
put the lable over an arrow.
Have a look at some of the existing diagrams
to decide whether you want to have white
or black text. The text colour should be the
one that reads best against whatever colour
is behind it.
You can also use the text colour to subtly
distinguish different components. For instance,
black text for components outside the scope of
whatever you are discussing, white text for
components in scope. This means, of course,
that your objects must be coloured
accordingly.
If you a switching text colour a lot, then
you probably need to rethink you colours.
Object with frames for sections. Use for things
such as HMI with two different UI technologies.
You will notice that these rectangles have drop
shadows, and that some of them have rounded
corners.
When you are working with objects that have
shadows, you may want to hide the shadows,
as they can make things difficult when you
are trying to select other objects nearby.
To do this, fromt he top menu, select Window,
then check the Appearance. You’ll get a widget
with all sorts of junk. Select your object,
and click the eye next to Drop Shadow to
toggle on and off.
If you want to change the details for the
drop shapow, double-click Drop Shadow and
adjust the details.
I use 40, 40% darkness.
If you are creating a new shape with
rounded corners, the best method
(I think) is to create the shape without
rounded corners, then add these afterwards.
This gives you more control over the
corners, in particular how they change
(or don’t) when you resize your shape.
Showing and tweaking rounded corners
is a variation on how you do said things
to drop shadows. Same widget.
